Every session viola starts names its model and effort: viola run, and the start arm of viola revive, hand the claude child a model and an effort on every spawn, the pair the operator gave or else viola's configured default pair.
The pair is recorded per instance as a closed set of values, beside the lineage record (events log, snapshot, replay).
viola revive replays the recorded pair on its resume, so a resumed session runs on the pair its instance recorded.
It re-measures at P3 the claude CLI channel for model and effort, and what a resume does with them today; it builds no inheritance for open, up or adopt, and writes nothing to the user's own settings.

The viola run argument surface and the viola revive start arm gain a model and an effort the operator may give; the viola --help usage and verb rows that list them stay served-verbs-only and pinned by literal.

The child spawn of claude carries the model and the effort on every start, through the channel (flag, environment name or settings key) P3 measures; the argv is built from the parsed arguments, never from typed-back text.

viola's configured default pair: where no pair is given the start uses the default; if the fork lands it in config.json, it is a new config.json key with a fixed name and closed set of values, read like the other config keys.
The pair is recorded per instance in the events log and the snapshot, as a closed set of values, and replayed on rebuild beside the lineage record.
viola revive's resume replays the instance's recorded pair onto the resumed claude child; a revive with no recorded pair (an instance from before this chunk) still resumes on the default.

A model or effort value outside the closed set is refused at the argument surface: a usage error with exit 2, or a refusal as unable line with a kebab-case code word beside it and one hint line, never a stack trace or bare status; under --json it is one clean failure document with no hint.

viola run, revive start and revive --json keep their existing refusal documents, start-refusal and revive --json refusal codes, exit codes and hint pairs unchanged while the pair is added to the start path.

viola list board, viola list --json and the MCP list tool: whether the pair is shown is a fork; if shown, it is a word in its own column with fixed caption order, never carried by colour alone, no SGR off a terminal or in --json.

During the TUI passthrough after the start, viola prints zero bytes of its own on the terminal; any diagnostic of the pair chosen or replayed goes to the run diagnostics log, never the terminal, with the log identity tags.
The user's own claude settings stay byte-identical: the chunk writes nothing to them and reads nothing of the operator's real home claude settings in this phase.
Fixed CLI strings the chunk adds (option help, refusal words, hints, any list caption) come from design copy and are pinned by literal tests; printed names are the parsed arguments.
The new start and revive behaviour is proved by tests sequenced on records and a stand-in child, never a live claude start; live readings never gate, and no time bound falls on the human.
The new tests run inside the existing suites as nextest failures, with no skips, zero flakiness and no retries, inside the coverage suite of the push/PR workflow; the gate breach fails the build.

body_fields.convention: each new fixed CLI string (help line, refusal word, hint, caption) is pinned by a literal test and comes from design copy
each new refusal names a kebab-case code word beside unable, carries exactly one hint (none for a fault), and under --json is one clean document
each new a11y-bearing test runs inside the existing test suites and fails as a nextest failure
each new test is deterministic, never skipped and never retried
each new test case runs inside the coverage suite of the GitHub Actions push/PR workflow, with no artifact or driver of its own
each new log line of a run goes to the run diagnostics, never the terminal, and carries the log identity tags

Every session viola starts names a model and an effort: `viola run` and the start arm of `viola revive` hand the claude child the pair the operator gave, else viola's configured default pair, on every spawn.
The pair is recorded per instance as a closed set of values, beside the lineage record in the events log and the snapshot, and `viola revive` replays the recorded pair on its resume.
The CLI channel that carries the pair to claude (a flag, an environment name or a settings key), where and in what shape the pair is recorded, and what a resume does with model and effort today are measured at P3 first, never assumed; an undocumented claude behaviour becomes a capability ledger row with a verify probe.
Whether the pair is shown on `viola list`, its --json and the MCP list tool, and whether the default pair lives in config.json, are forks of the operator's; nothing is written to the user's own settings.

The `viola run` and `viola revive` argument surface gains model and effort inputs: CLI input crosses the trust boundary and is checked as a closed set of values before anything is read, spawned or framed; a bad value is refused whole, never stripped or narrowed.

The claude child spawn carries the pair on every start: the values go to the child as argv elements with no shell, resolved by the same child resolution that run and revive use today, and the pair is a closed value, never free text from upstream.

If the CLI channel measured at P3 is an environment name, the child environment rules bind it: parent identity variables and inherited CLAUDE credentials stay stripped, the environment is not a configuration channel for viola itself, a new environment read or seam needs its log entry, and the process-start claude-child line records env names only, never CLAUDE values.

A default pair in config.json, if the fork lands there: the config is parsed tolerantly, a bad value falls back by the bad-config-values rule rather than reaching the child, and no config value may switch off a control.

The per-instance record of the pair in the events log and the snapshot: kept to those two stores as the lineage record is, written only by the instance's own wrapper, owner-only modes, plaintext protected by OS permissions, a closed set of values so readers tolerate torn lines and unknown values.

Revive's replay of the recorded pair: the snapshot is read only after the strict-modes check of the home and the snapshot, the replayed value is re-checked against the closed set and falls back by the replayed-snapshot fallbacks when it does not parse, and a replayed snapshot still runs nothing and frames nothing beyond the spawn.

The start arm of revive and run keep their existing check order: strict modes and the socket-directory check before any bind, snapshot or child; the new inputs add refusals that come after the instance and home checks, not before them.

New refusals of a bad model or effort value on run and revive: fixed messages that interpolate nothing, no paths, pids or ids, sanitised for human output, and a closed code on the revive --json error document if one is added.

If the pair is shown on `viola list`, list --json or the MCP list tool: the board shows a recorded value only when it re-parses to the closed set, human output escapes control characters, and the client screens the server's answer to closed values.

Nothing is written under the Claude home or into the user's own settings: the pair reaches the child only through the measured CLI channel, keeping v2-31's promise that the user's settings stay byte-identical reachable.

The capability ledger row for an undocumented claude behaviour, with its verify probe: the probe reads signatures only, compares against compiled literals, answers no dialog and keeps its effects in its own directory; this phase runs no live start, no rig start of a real claude and reads nothing of the operator's real Claude home.
The P3 measurements run without a real claude in CI: the real claude CLI is local only, CI holds no secrets, and any fixture recorded from the child is scrubbed and reviewed before commit.
Tests of the new pair handling reach the child through the fake agent: test seams live only under the fake-agent feature and are compiled out of the release build.

The viola run and viola revive argument surface: new arguments naming a model and an effort, tested as a subprocess, with negative cases for bad or out-of-set values on the CLI and env vectors.

viola's configured default pair: a config key for the default model and effort, where a missing or bad value falls back to its default rather than failing the start.
The per-instance record of the pair as a closed set of values: a closed enum changes only by a logged decision, and an unknown value read back is refused or skipped, never guessed.

viola revive: the resume replays the recorded pair, its preflight order and refusal codes and exit codes stay as they are, and a revived child runs on the recorded pair rather than the default.
